life_summary: Patrick Richard Kearon was born on July 18, 1961, in Carlisle, England. He grew up in post-war England and pursued education and professional development that prepared him for humanitarian and ecclesiastical leadership. Before his full-time Church service, Kearon worked in humanitarian and social justice contexts, developing expertise in refugee assistance, human rights protection, and supporting survivors of violence and oppression. He married Jennifer Carole Hulme in 1991 at the Oakland California Temple after meeting her, a BYU student, in London. The couple has four children, though their eldest child passed away at three weeks old from a heart condition—an experience that deepened their compassion for suffering families. His professional background in humanitarian work informed his subsequent Church leadership.
church_summary: Kearon began full-time service in the Church as a general authority in 2010, bringing his humanitarian expertise to Church assignments. He was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 2018. His ministry has emphasized religious freedom and protecting the rights of all people regardless of faith background, spiritual healing through Jesus Christ's atonement, humanitarian service particularly regarding refugee assistance, and supporting survivors of abuse, violence, and oppression. His personal experience with grief and his professional background in humanitarian work have enabled him to address the needs of vulnerable and marginalized populations with particular compassion and understanding, making him a voice for the suffering and dispossessed.
teaching_emphasis: Compassion for the suffering and vulnerable
